Don't know if it's true but it demonstrates what I'm talking about. He had a vision for what the iPod should be, was not satisifed with what was available, but noticed that there had to be room for improvement.

These people are few and far between. A friendlier example might be Henry Kloss - Accoustic Research, KLH, Advent, Cambridge Soundworks.

Kloss had a vision for high fidelity audio and created it, but he believed it should be something affordable to everyone and he made sure that was possible.

(An example from Cambridge Soundworks is the P1000 subwoofer. In order to get deep, accurate bass, you need a large surface area for the woofer. But a large speaker needs a large cabinet and no one really wants a giant ugly box sitting around their living room. The enclosure had options for real wood veneers - mahogany and beech, as well as a neutral gray. This made it look very nice. Too get the deep bass, Instead of a single woofer, it has two 10 inchers opposite each other, facing outwards. Because of their facing, the enclosure will not rattle. Two 10" woofers have almost the same surface area as a single 15" and up from that size, there's little practical advantage. But with two woofers, you need more power so it was given a very complicated hybrid type of amplifier called B.A.S.H. IT allowed for 1000 watts of peak output - that is, it doesn't draw 1000 watts from the wall, it has capacitors that allowed it to burst power as needed. Subwoofers are notorious for being hard to place in a room and long cord runs can result in noise getting into the line. The ended up forgoeing the traditional amplifier sub out -> subwoofer. Instead, you ran the sub out to a break-out box and the breakout box ran a balanced line out to the subwoofer. The balanced line makes sure you don't pick up noise. The kicker, is that the balanced line is just a traditional telephone cord - no fancy expensive equipment. Another nicety, and you have to keep in mind that this was back in the days of CRTs which were sensitive to magnets, was that the whole enclosure was EM shielded - the enclosure is a faraday cage.

Anyway, this thing, and I do own one... ok maybe two... was only $1,000 when it was brand new. It got down to half that price before it was eventually discontinued. For the price and performance, there just wasn't anything close and especially not something that as thoroughly took into account design decision. This was the first subwoofer that made reallly appreciate bass; the thing SINGS the low notes. It doesn't, however, like to be a home theater subwoofer. I mean, it does its job absolutely fine, but movie special effects are not the same as music.)
